\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{катер} (káter)}{катер (káter)}]{\ru{катер} (káter) — a motor boat, a launch}

\label{lesson:RU-C426-kater}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for to make seasick or carsick, then the Russian for an anchor.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{катер}}
\textbf{\ru{катер}} (\emph{káter}) — \textquotedblleft{}a motor boat, a launch\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ru{На} \ru{катере} \ru{мы} \ru{быстро} \ru{добрались} \ru{до} \ru{острова}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Na kátere my býstro dobrális do óstrova.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We quickly got to the island by motor boat.
\end{quote}

Masculine; plural \emph{\ru{катера}}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{\ru{катер}} was borrowed from English \emph{cutter} (EtymDB), a small fast boat, built on \emph{cut}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{káter}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{káter}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Russian for to make seasick or carsick, then the Russian for an anchor, then say \emph{káter} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{шлюпка} (shlyúpka)}{шлюпка (shlyúpka)}]{\ru{шлюпка} (shlyúpka) — a ship's boat, a lifeboat}

\label{lesson:RU-C426-shlyupka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for an anchor, then the Russian for a motor boat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{шлюпка}}
\textbf{\ru{шлюпка}} (\emph{shlyúpka}) — \textquotedblleft{}a ship's boat, a lifeboat\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ru{На} \ru{корабле} \ru{есть} \ru{шлюпки} \ru{для} \ru{всех} \ru{пассажиров}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Na korablé yest shlyúpki dlya vsekh passazhírov.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There are lifeboats on the ship for all the passengers.
\end{quote}

Feminine. \emph{\ru{Спасательная} \ru{шлюпка}} — a lifeboat.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{\ru{шлюпка}} is a diminutive of \emph{\ru{шлюп}} 'a sloop' (EtymDB lists \emph{\ru{шлюп}}), which is usually traced to Dutch \emph{sloep}, a word EtymDB links with a Middle Dutch verb for gliding.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Russian for an anchor, then the Russian for a motor boat, then say \emph{shlyúpka} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{жилет} (zhilét)}{жилет (zhilét)}]{\ru{жилет} (zhilét) — a waistcoat; a vest (\ru{спасательный} \ru{жилет}: a life jacket)}

\label{lesson:RU-C426-zhilet}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for a motor boat, then the Russian for a ship's boat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{жилет}}
\textbf{\ru{жилет}} (\emph{zhilét}) — \textquotedblleft{}a waistcoat; a vest (\ru{спасательный} \ru{жилет}: a life jacket)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ru{Всем} \ru{дали} \ru{спасательные} \ru{жилеты} \ru{перед} \ru{прогулкой} \ru{на} \ru{лодке}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Vsem dáli spasátelnyye zhiléty péred progúlkoy na lódke.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Everyone was given a life jacket before the boat trip.
\end{quote}

Masculine. \emph{\ru{Спасательный} \ru{жилет}} — a life jacket.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{\ru{жилет}} was borrowed from French \emph{gilet} 'a waistcoat' (EtymDB), a word EtymDB traces further to Arabic.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{весло} (vesló)}{весло (vesló)}]{\ru{весло} (vesló) — an oar, a paddle}

\label{lesson:RU-C426-veslo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for a ship's boat, then the Russian for a waistcoat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{весло}}
\textbf{\ru{весло}} (\emph{vesló}) — \textquotedblleft{}an oar, a paddle\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ru{У} \ru{лодки} \ru{было} \ru{только} \ru{одно} \ru{весло}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{U lódki býlo tólko odnó vesló.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The boat had only one oar.
\end{quote}

Neuter; plural \emph{\ru{вёсла}}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{\ru{весло}} is inherited through Old East Slavic \emph{veslo} from Proto-Slavic \emph{veslo} 'an oar' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{грести} (grestí)}{грести (grestí)}]{\ru{грести} (grestí) — to row; to rake}

\label{lesson:RU-C426-gresti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for a waistcoat, then the Russian for an oar.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{грести}}
\textbf{\ru{грести}} (\emph{grestí}) — \textquotedblleft{}to row; to rake\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ru{Отец} \ru{гребёт}, \ru{а} \ru{мы} \ru{сидим} \ru{и} \ru{отдыхаем}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Otéts grebyót, a my sidím i otdykháyem.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Dad rows, and we sit and rest.
\end{quote}

Imperfective. Present \emph{\ru{гребу}, \ru{гребёшь}}; past \emph{\ru{грёб}, \ru{гребла}}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{\ru{грести}} is inherited from Proto-Slavic \emph{greti} 'to dig, to scrape, to rake' (EtymDB): an oar pulls through water as a rake pulls through soil.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Russian for a waistcoat, then the Russian for an oar, then say \emph{grestí} again

\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 419–426 — a review}

\label{lesson:RU-R426-review-419-426}



\begin{quote}
Say the Russian for check-in and to check in.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item check-in, to check in, a flight, luggage, boarding
  \item a security check, to search, a border guard, a customs declaration, to declare
  \item to take off, take-off, to land, a porthole, the steps
  \item a departure, to fly out, an arrival, a terminal, a flight attendant
  \item a delay, to delay, a cancellation, to cancel, compensation
  \item a ferry, a deck, a cabin, a mooring, a landing stage
  \item to sail off, to moor, the rolling, to make seasick or carsick, an anchor
  \item a motor boat, a ship's boat, a waistcoat, an oar, to row
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Check-in? (\textbf{\ru{регистрация}}.) To check in? (\textbf{\ru{регистрироваться}}.) A flight? (\textbf{\ru{рейс}}.) Luggage? (\textbf{\ru{кладь}}.) Boarding? (\textbf{\ru{посадочный}}.) A security check? (\textbf{\ru{досмотр}}.) To search? (\textbf{\ru{досматривать}}.) A border guard? (\textbf{\ru{пограничник}}.) A customs declaration? (\textbf{\ru{декларация}}.) To declare? (\textbf{\ru{декларировать}}.) To take off? (\textbf{\ru{взлетать}}.) Take-off? (\textbf{\ru{взлёт}}.) To land? (\textbf{\ru{приземляться}}.) A porthole? (\textbf{\ru{иллюминатор}}.) The steps? (\textbf{\ru{трап}}.) A departure? (\textbf{\ru{вылет}}.) To fly out? (\textbf{\ru{вылетать}}.) An arrival? (\textbf{\ru{прилёт}}.) A terminal? (\textbf{\ru{терминал}}.) A flight attendant? (\textbf{\ru{стюардесса}}.) A delay? (\textbf{\ru{задержка}}.) To delay? (\textbf{\ru{задерживать}}.) A cancellation? (\textbf{\ru{отмена}}.) To cancel? (\textbf{\ru{отменять}}.) Compensation? (\textbf{\ru{компенсация}}.) A ferry? (\textbf{\ru{паром}}.) A deck? (\textbf{\ru{палуба}}.) A cabin? (\textbf{\ru{каюта}}.) A mooring? (\textbf{\ru{причал}}.) A landing stage? (\textbf{\ru{пристань}}.) To sail off? (\textbf{\ru{отплывать}}.) To moor? (\textbf{\ru{причаливать}}.) The rolling? (\textbf{\ru{качка}}.) To make seasick or carsick? (\textbf{\ru{укачивать}}.) An anchor? (\textbf{\ru{якорь}}.) A motor boat? (\textbf{\ru{катер}}.) A ship's boat? (\textbf{\ru{шлюпка}}.) A waistcoat? (\textbf{\ru{жилет}}.) An oar? (\textbf{\ru{весло}}.) To row? (\textbf{\ru{грести}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
